items.readable_text:
Content:
We need to be extra careful when converting from one unit of area to another.

Content:
To demonstrate, suppose that a square has an area of [MATH: 2\,\textrm{cm}^2.] Let's use unit arguments to express this area in square millimeters.

Content:
We start by recalling the conversion table for units of length.

Content:
| Name | Symbol | Conversion |
| Kilometer | [MATH: \textrm{km}] | [MATH: 1\,\textrm{km} = 1\,000\,\textrm{m}] |
| Meter | [MATH: \textrm{m}] | Base Unit |
| Centimeter | [MATH: \textrm{cm}] | [MATH: 100\,\textrm{cm} = 1\,\textrm{m}] |
| Millimeter | [MATH: \textrm{mm}] | [MATH: 10\,\textrm{mm} = 1\,\textrm{cm}] |

Content:
Since we're converting from [MATH: \textrm{cm}^2] to [MATH: \textrm{mm}^2], we start with the conversion between [MATH: \textrm{cm}] and [MATH: \textrm{mm}]. According to our table, there are [MATH: 10\,\textrm{mm}] per [MATH: \textrm{cm}.] We can write this ratio as a fraction, as follows:

Content:
[MATH: \dfrac{10\,\textrm{mm}}{\textrm{cm}}]

Content:
Watch Out! This is not the conversion factor we need. If we multiply [MATH: 2\,\textrm{cm}^2] by this conversion factor, we will not get an equivalent area!

Content:
The problem with using this conversion factor is that it does not contain area units. However, we can convert this into area units by squaring it and applying the rules of exponents as follows:

Content:
[MATH: ((10mm)/(cm))^{2}|= (10^{2}mm^{2})/(cm^{2}); = (100mm^{2})/(cm^{2})]

Content:
This is now the correct conversion factor. It tells us that there are [MATH: 100] square millimeters per square centimeter.

Content:
Now, multiplying [MATH: 2\,\textrm{cm}^2] by our conversion factor, we get

Content:
[MATH: 2cm^{2}|= 2cm^{2} ⋅ (100mm^{2})/(cm^{2}); = 2cm^{2} ⋅ (100mm^{2})/(cm^{2}); = 2 ⋅ 100mm^{2}; = 200mm^{2}.]

Content:
Therefore, we conclude that [MATH: 2\,\textrm{cm}^2] is equivalent to [MATH: 200\,\textrm{mm}^2.]

Earlier, we calculated that [MATH: 1\,\textrm{cm}^2] is equivalent to [MATH: 100\,\textrm{mm}^2.] Let's try to understand this computation intuitively.

Content:
When we convert the units of length from [MATH: \textrm{cm}] to [MATH: \textrm{mm},] we essentially partition the length and width of this square into [MATH: 10] equal parts. Doing this, we partition the square into [MATH: 10^2 = 100] equally-sized smaller squares.

sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
There are [MATH: 10\,\textrm{mm}] per [MATH: \textrm{cm},] which we can write as follows: [MATH: \dfrac{10\,\textrm{mm}}{\textrm{cm}}]

We need to convert this into area units. So, by squaring this quantity and applying the rules of exponents, we get [MATH: ((10mm)/(cm))^{2}|= (10^{2}mm^{2})/(cm^{2}); = (100mm^{2})/(cm^{2}).]

This is our conversion factor.

Now, multiplying [MATH: 3.4 \, \textrm{cm}^2] by our conversion factor, we get [MATH: 3.4cm^{2}|= 3.4cm^{2} ⋅ (100mm^{2})/(cm^{2}); = 3.4cm^{2} ⋅ (100mm^{2})/(cm^{2}); = 3.4 ⋅ 100mm^{2}; = 340mm^{2}.]

Therefore, [MATH: 3.4\,\textrm{cm}^2] is equivalent to [MATH: 340\,\textrm{mm}^2.]

Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Content:
We need to be extra careful when converting from one unit of area to another.

Content:

Content:
| Name | Symbol | Conversion |

| Meter | [MATH: \textrm{m}] | Base Unit |
| Centimeter | [MATH: \textrm{cm}] | [MATH: 100\,\textrm{cm} = 1\,\textrm{m}] |
| Millimeter | [MATH: \textrm{mm}] | [MATH: 10\,\textrm{mm} = 1\,\textrm{cm}] |

Content:
Since we're converting from [MATH: \textrm{cm}^2] to [MATH: \textrm{mm}^2], we start with the conversion between [MATH: \textrm{cm}] and [MATH: \textrm{mm}]. According to our table, there are [MATH: 10\,\textrm{mm}] per [MATH: \textrm{cm}.] We can write this ratio as a fraction, as follows:

Content:
[MATH: \dfrac{10\,\textrm{mm}}{\textrm{cm}}]

Content:
Watch Out! This is not the conversion factor we need. If we multiply [MATH: 2\,\textrm{cm}^2] by this conversion factor, we will not get an equivalent area!

Content:
The problem with using this conversion factor is that it does not contain area units. However, we can convert this into area units by squaring it and applying the rules of exponents as follows:

Content:
[MATH: ((10mm)/(cm))^{2}|= (10^{2}mm^{2})/(cm^{2}); = (100mm^{2})/(cm^{2})]

Content:
This is now the correct conversion factor. It tells us that there are [MATH: 100] square millimeters per square centimeter.

Content:
Now, multiplying [MATH: 2\,\textrm{cm}^2] by our conversion factor, we get

Content:
[MATH: 2cm^{2}|= 2cm^{2} ⋅ (100mm^{2})/(cm^{2}); = 2cm^{2} ⋅ (100mm^{2})/(cm^{2}); = 2 ⋅ 100mm^{2}; = 200mm^{2}.]

Content:
Therefore, we conclude that [MATH: 2\,\textrm{cm}^2] is equivalent to [MATH: 200\,\textrm{mm}^2.]

---

Content:
Earlier, we calculated that [MATH: 1\,\textrm{cm}^2] is equivalent to [MATH: 100\,\textrm{mm}^2.] Let's try to understand this computation intuitively.
